question: As of July 2025, how many total Ramsar Sites does India has?
solution:
The correct answer is __**4) 91**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• As of **July 2025**, India has a total of **91 Ramsar Sites**, which are wetlands of international importance under the **Ramsar Convention**. 
• The Ramsar Convention was signed in **1971 in Ramsar, Iran**, and India is one of its signatories, committed to the conservation and sustainable use of wetlands. 
• The **total area covered** by these Ramsar Sites in India is approximately **1.8 million hectares**, spanning various ecosystems such as mangroves, lakes, rivers, and marshes. 
• Examples of significant Ramsar Sites in India include **Keoladeo National Park (Rajasthan)**, **Loktak Lake (Manipur)**, and **Sundarbans Wetland (West Bengal)**. 
• India has made substantial progress in wetland conservation, with the **addition of 50 new Ramsar Sites since 2019**, demonstrating its commitment to ecological preservation. 
• The inclusion of a wetland as a Ramsar Site ensures **international recognition** and emphasizes its **protection and sustainable use**. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 
• **Ramsar Convention:** 
• The **Ramsar Convention** is an international treaty adopted on **February 2, 1971**, to ensure the conservation and sustainable use of wetlands. 
• It aims to prevent the degradation of wetlands and is celebrated as **World Wetlands Day** annually on **February 2**. 
• Globally, there are over **2,500 Ramsar Sites**, highlighting the importance of wetland conservation worldwide. 
• **Criteria for Ramsar Sites:** 
• To qualify as a Ramsar Site, a wetland must meet at least **one of the nine criteria** related to biodiversity, ecological significance, or cultural importance. 
• These criteria include supporting **vulnerable species**, maintaining **ecological diversity**, or hosting large populations of birds and fish. 
• **India’s Achievements:** 
• India has added **50 new Ramsar Sites since 2019**, showcasing its dedication to wetland conservation. 
• The **largest Ramsar Site** in India is the **Sundarbans Wetland**, while the **smallest** is the **Renuka Wetland** in Himachal Pradesh. 
• **Importance of Wetlands:** 
• Wetlands act as **natural water filters**, help in **flood control**, and support **biodiversity**. 
• They play a vital role in **carbon sequestration**, making them crucial in combating climate change. 
• **Key Indian Initiatives:** 
• The **National Plan for Conservation of Aquatic Ecosystems (NPCA)** is a government initiative aimed at protecting and managing wetlands and lakes in India. 
• The **Wetlands (Conservation and Management) Rules, 2017** provide a legal framework for wetland conservation in India. 
• **International Cooperation:** 
• Through the Ramsar Convention, India collaborates with other nations to share **knowledge** and **best practices** for wetland conservation.
